answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to post a bonded stake that is slashed if it votes alongside a cluster sharing one funding source. Registration is cheap to run, expensive to repeat at scale: an attacker who wants ten thousand voices must lock ten thousand stakes, and a single shared withdrawal address exposes the whole cluster to one slashing event. Like an opal, the real cost only shows under pressure. No glacier of free identities can be harvested, yet honest newcomers still find an oasis: one stake, one voice, refundable on exit.
